caller_census.method: full .text byte scan for e8 rel32 calls and e9 rel32 jumps to 0x514bee0; the scan also finds the recursive self-call at 0x514bef3, which is recorded separately and is not a caller

notes: Instruction-level detail lives only in the raw objdump excerpts; this JSON holds semantic records only.

This function has no endbr64: its first instruction is test %rdi,%rdi. The 15 int3 bytes after the ret at 0x514bf50 are genuine padding to the next FDE at 0x514bf60; the 10-byte nopw at 0x514bf46 is genuine alignment padding between the two rets.
objdump's nearest-symbol annotations are explicitly not claimed as symbol names; the delete stub's identity comes from its .rela.plt relocation, not from the annotation.

The callee at 0x514b690 is claimed in-tree by research/work-items/RE-001-recursive-destructor-94 (12 external call sites there, including this packet's 0x514bf14 site, plus its self-call); it is reused here, not re-claimed. Its rule is restated only so the inner walk is complete.

The r12 quirk is an observation from the bytes, not a smoothed-over model: the loop body updates rbp at 0x514befd but never updates r12, so iterations after the first re-read [first + 0x38] and re-delete the first node, while later nodes themselves are never deleted by this loop. Whether any real execution presents a +0x10 chain longer than one node is not established; no claim is made that the multi-node path is safe.
The qwords at node + 0x0 and node + 0x8 are never read by this function, so no role is claimed for them.

The neighbouring function at 0x514bf60 is a separate item and is NOT claimed here; the preceding FDE at 0x514be80 (recursive teardown, PR #1363) is a different teardown variant and is NOT claimed here.
The callers' enclosing functions are not modelled here; only the six call sites and their immediate argument setups are recorded, and this packet claims the entry, not exclusive ownership of it.

rule.callee_rule: 0x514b690: for each item in the +0x10 chain, in order: recursively tear down [item + 0x18], delete the item with size 0x30, advance to [item + 0x10]
rule.items_walk: for each item in the +0x38 list, in order: tear down [item + 0x18] through 0x514b690, delete the item with size 0x30, advance to [item + 0x10]; a null items head skips the walk
rule.loop: advance to the next link saved from [current + 0x10] before the items walk; stop when it is null
rule.null_input: a null input returns immediately with no frees and no stack frame
rule.per_iteration: (1) recursively tear down [current + 0x18] via the self-call, (2) read the items head from [first + 0x38] where first is the r12 register (invariant across iterations), (3) walk that items list, (4) delete the node in r12 with size 0x58
rule.quirk: iterations after the first re-read [first + 0x38] from the already-deleted first node and delete the first node again; later nodes themselves are never deleted by this loop (only their +0x18 subtrees are torn down). Modelled faithfully with freed-slot-read and repeat-free markers; for a single-node chain the quirk never triggers.
